items.title: 52222_Marshall Royal oral history interview
items.q: I played on his record, "The Sunny Side of the Street," with Eddie Haywood and so he immediately wanted to hire me. So, he did on the spot

ctx.x: Right, Hal Stanley owned it. Then, after about a week, Eddie Haywood called me up -- no, Lionel Hampton came in town and wanted me to reenter his band. So he set up a deal wherein I was supposed to meet him and after really thinking about it, I wasn't just sure whether I actually wanted to go back with Lionel Hampton or not, because he had incorporated so much marching into his band that that really didn't interest me because I was more musical-minded and I didn't dig walking through the aisles, parading, with…

When I did, I went out that evening and we made a recording and I played on his record, "The Sunny Side of the Street," with Eddie Haywood and so he immediately wanted to hire me. So, he did on the spot and I didn't go back to Lionel Hampton anymore to do any marching --
